Subject: Quick question on POC pricing and surge protection

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Samir and I were impressed with the latency numbers. We're close to greenlighting a 6-week POC, but procurement asked for two clarifications before we proceed: a) an alternative discount ladder if we commit to a small paid pilot (we're thinking $45k-$60k), and b) a protection mechanism for bursty usage — either a capped surge pool or a small overage credit model.

Can you share options that balance predictability for us and minimal downside for Redwood? Also, if there's a short SOW you can share with the pricing scenarios that would help procurement move quickly.

Appreciate it — aiming to finalize by next Friday.

Best,
Alicia

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on POC pricing and surge protection

Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Below are three practical options we can put into the SOW; I'm copying Naomi (pricing) and Connor (solutions) so they can add technical and billing details.

Option A — Timebox + Fixed Discount Ladder (recommended)
- 6-week POC priced at $50,000 fixed (covers up to an agreed token/hour baseline).
- Discount ladder if you convert to a 12-month reserved commitment within 30 days: 10% at $250k, 15% at $500k, 20% at $1M.
- Surge protection: one-time surge buffer of 10% of baseline included; overages billed at a reduced overage rate (25% discount to list).

Option B — Pay-as-you-go + Surge Cap
- PAYG unit rates (hosted) with an explicit surge cap set in the Console.
- Once cap is reached, requests are queued/fallback to a lower-cost variant; we provide a weekly usage dashboard.
- No upfront discount; can add a conversion credit toward committed tier if you convert within 60 days.

Option C — Small Commitment + Credits
- $45k prepay credited against usage; additional usage billed at a discounted rate.
- Surge handled by a pre-funded burst bucket ($5k) that kicks in automatically; any excess billed monthly.

I'll attach a draft SOW and a simple spreadsheet with modeled cost scenarios for each. If one of these looks good, Naomi will formalize the pricing and I can spin up the requested surge simulations with Connor.

Next steps: which option would procurement prefer to see in a formal SOW? Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: POC_Pricing_Options.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Hi Alicia — quick follow to add concrete numbers for Option A (Mateo's recommended path). I did a short cost model based on your post-demo token profile. Key points:

- 6-week POC (Fixed Price): $50,000 covers up to 1.8M tokens total (~avg 150k tokens/week).
- Surge buffer: 10% (180k tokens) included. Excess tokens billed at $0.0009/token (25% off our standard eval rate).
- Conversion credit: If you sign a 12-month Reserved within 30 days, we'll credit up to $8k toward the first invoice (applies to commitments >= $250k).

Attachments: I've uploaded a short SOW (Fathom_SOW_draft.docx) and a tabbed workbook with three traffic scenarios. Connor — on the technical side, if Fathom expects heavy bursts (e.g., ingest-driven peaks) we can pre-stage cached responses for top-20 prompts and reserve a burst slice — happy to outline the ops steps.

Alicia — if procurement wants the surge as a pre-funded bucket instead of per-token overage, we can flip to Option C and show the math. Which do you prefer for the SOW?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Pricing & Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
